title: On‑Prem Contract Playbook & Negotiation Templates for Regulated Buyers
content:
Purpose: practical negotiation-ready language and short GTM scripts to help field teams (AE, solutions, legal, security) move on‑prem / VPC control plane deals with regulated buyers. Focus: reduce review cycles, limit legal counterproposals, and give sales prescriptive concessions and tradeoffs.

Executive summary:
- Typical friction for regulated buyers: auditability, data residency, incident response, access controls, indemnity & liability caps, and where the control plane lives.
- Goal: provide standard clause templates, a prioritized concession ladder (what to give away and what to hold), and short customer-facing scripts for procurement/security to accelerate approval.
- Outcome: 1–2 week reduction in average contract negotiation time on net-new private deploy deals if teams use these templates as a baseline.

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Start with the ‘standard clause’ block in section A as our baseline.
2) For each customer, map their primary risk bucket (privacy, IP, uptime, compliance) and select the matching negotiation ladder from section B.
3) Use one of the short scripts in section C for discovery/first pass with the security/ procurement team.
4) For legal, attach the lightweight appendix with audit scope + SOC2/KMS references and vendor responsibility matrix.

A. Standard clause language (to insert in SOW/MSA drafts) — copy/paste candidates (internal use):
- Data Residency and Processing: "Customer Data (including logs and telemetry) will be stored and processed in the customer’s VPC or on‑premises infrastructure under Customer control. Redwood Inference’s control plane will not persist Customer Data outside Customer infrastructure except as explicitly agreed in writing. Where Redwood operates a management/control plane component, all persisted Customer Data will be encrypted at rest using keys provided by Customer KMS (bring-your-own-key)."
- Audit & Inspection Rights: "Customer shall have the right, upon reasonable notice and during normal business hours, to perform (a) remote automated audits of configuration and access logs, and (b) one on‑site audit per 12 months or as required by regulation. Redwood will cooperate and provide reasonable access to evidence required to validate compliance with the SOW. For sensitive or air-gapped environments, Redwood will accept attestations from authorized third-party auditors in lieu of on‑site visits."
- Incident Response & Notification: "Redwood will notify Customer within 24 hours of Redwood’s detection of a suspected security incident affecting Customer Data or production systems that could materially impact confidentiality, integrity, or availability. Redwood will provide a post‑incident report within 10 business days containing root cause, remediation steps, and risk mitigation actions. For high severity incidents impacting personal data, Redwood will support Customer’s regulatory notification obligations."
- Access & Separation: "Redwood will not access Customer Data for any purpose other than providing the contracted services, performing support with Customer authorization, or as legally compelled. Access to Customer systems by Redwood staff requires multi‑party authorization and is logged and auditable. Non‑interactive support tools shall be scoped to minimum necessary privileges."
- Liability & Indemnity (balanced starter): "Each party’s aggregate liability for breach arising under this Agreement shall be capped at the total amounts paid by Customer to Redwood under the Agreement in the prior 12 months, except for liability resulting from willful misconduct or gross negligence, and except for breaches of confidentiality or data protection obligations, for which a higher cap (or no cap) may be specified by mutual agreement. Redwood will indemnify Customer for third‑party claims alleging Redwood’s infringement of patents or copyrights related to the software provided."
- Escrow option (for very large regulated customers): "Customer may require source code escrow and evidence of build/release reproducibility for the control plane component, subject to separate escrow agreement and fees."

Note: these are starting points — coordinate with legal if customer redlines more than two of the above sections.

B. Negotiation ladder: prioritized concessions and tradeoffs (sales playbook)
- Tiering by ask severity and suggested response (quick):
  * Ask: Uncapped liability for any breach.
    - Response: Reject in principle; offer higher cap for data-protection breaches only + buy‑down via insurance certificate (cyber).
  * Ask: Full source access / IP assignment.
    - Response: Offer escrow + reproducible build + stronger indemnity for IP claims. No IP assignment.
  * Ask: Unlimited on‑site audits & live access to logs.
    - Response: Offer quarterly remote audits + one annual on‑site + redacted logs for sensitive items. Third-party auditor OK.
  * Ask: Control plane must be run in buyer-managed VMs only (no Redwood-managed components).
    - Response: Evaluate feasibility. If feasible, offer hybrid control plane with management APIs limited to telemetry and orchestration; customer pays integration fee. Otherwise offer strict data segregation + BYOK for keys + transparent telemetry schema.
  * Ask: SLA with financial credits for every minute of downtime.
    - Response: Offer tiered SLOs with availability measurement method + capped service credits (e.g., percentage of monthly fee), not unlimited credits. Extra reliability guarantees can be supplied on Dedicated plans.

Tradeoff guidance: the fastest way to win is to accept operational controls (BYOK, audit evidence, extra logging) rather than big monetary concessions. Monetary concessions are last resort.

C. Short scripts — use in initial security/procurement calls (30–60s soundbites):
- Security/Engineering: "We run the control plane with a minimal footprint in your VPC and we never persist customer payloads outside your network by default. For telemetry and health we can provide a sanitized schema and a separate logging pipeline to your SIEM. We can also accept BYOK and support a managed KMS integration — which part of your stack should own the keys?"
- Procurement/Legal: "We have a standard private deployment MSA with a handful of clauses buyers typically ask about — liability, audit, and data residency. To keep review cycles short, we recommend starting from our baseline and only negotiating the two highest priority items you surface; we can accommodate audit-by-third-party and escrow in scoped addenda."
- CISO/Compliance: "We provide SOC2 reports and can arrange a tailored evidence package for controls around access, change management, and incident response. If you need on‑prem air‑gapped deployment we have a proven checklist and a partner flow for validations."

D. Procurement checklist & doc pack to attach to RFP/SOW (one‑pager items):
- Standard attachments: SOC2 Type II, ISO attestation (if available), list of subservice providers, Vulnerability disclosure policy, third‑party penetration test summary.
- Technical attachments: network diagram for hybrid control plane, minimal privileged roles matrix, KMS integration instructions, sample configuration for telemetry redaction.
- Commercial attachments: sample SOW with clear deliverables, migration/offboarding plan, optional escrow agreement.

E. Competitive framing vs alternatives (short bullets for pitches):
- Versus hosted API: "We bring the same developer UX and APIs to your VPC with enterprise-grade controls — you get performance and predictability without sacrificing residency and audit visibility."
- Versus pure self‑hosted (customer builds): "Compared to building in‑house, we deliver a hardened runtime with continuous optimizations (batching, KV cache, kernel selection) plus operational playbooks — so you avoid multi‑quarter infra projects and get predictable unit economics."
- Versus other private deployment vendors: "We emphasize a small management plane footprint, BYOK, and a clear handoff for audit evidence. If audit transparency is your priority, our data‑separation patterns and telemetries are designed to minimize security friction."

F. Pricing knobs & concession economics (notes for AE and finance):
- Common levers: sign‑term discounts, integration/time-and-materials for hybrid work, separate fees for escrow and extra audit days, uplift for guaranteed Dedicated capacity/SLA.
- Play: trade a 6–8 week delivery guarantee and a small premium for refusing uncapped liability and IP assignment. Offer more evidence and tooling instead of lowering liability caps.

G. Redlines we accept without exec signoff (quick list):
- Add one annual on‑site audit (or third‑party), remote evidence sharing, additional defined logging retention, acceptance of BYOK for control plane persisted secrets, providing SOC2 artifact copies.

H. Redlines that require legal/finance/exec escalation:
- Uncapped liability, IP assignment, wholesale changes to indemnity for Redwood software beyond data claims, requests for full source transfer without escrow fee.

I. Field play examples (mini case studies) — anonymized:
- Large fintech: wanted strict data residency + 24/7 audit. Outcome: hybrid control plane, BYOK, quarterly remote audits + 2 annual on‑site days. Added 12% professional services fee for the integration work; legal accepted capped liability for data breaches with cyber insurance evidence.
- Healthcare customer: required escrow + explicit build reproducibility. Outcome: escrow agreement + annual build verification run by customer engineer; Redwood supplied golden images and a reproducible CI script.

J. Quick FAQ (for AE / SE):
- Q: Do we ever accept full source code handover?
  A: Only via escrow for business‑critical customers and with a separate escrow agreement and fees.
- Q: Can we operate entirely without any Redwood-managed control plane?
  A: In most cases we can offer a hybrid where orchestration is done via customer-managed components; fully removing the management plane increases integration time and cost.

K. TODOs / Open questions (notes to internal team):
- Finalize a standard escrow template with legal.
- Create a short one‑page security evidence pack tailored for healthcare & finance.
- Build a sample BYOK integration guide and internal checklist for SRE-run installs.
- Gather insurance certificate template language for sales to present as mitigation.

Appendix: example audit scope snippet to attach to SOW (copy/paste):
"Scope: Redwood will provide access to configuration and access logs for the Redwood-managed components of the deployment limited to the Customer tenant/namespace. The scope excludes Redwood internal operational metrics and developer tooling unrelated to Customer runtime. Redwood will provide evidence of: user role mappings, privileged access logs, change control tickets for configuration changes affecting Customer, and vulnerability remediation timelines for high/critical issues."

Notes to self: keep this doc lean — field teams prefer checklists and copy/paste language. We should convert into a one‑page cheat sheet + a short Confluence playbook (linked) and a repo with contract snippets for legal to import into DocuSign templates.
